what_it_does: This paper describes a flash LiDAR sensor—a camera that measures distance by sending pulses of laser light and timing how long they take to return. The challenge is achieving both good depth resolution and flexible frame rates while handling bright backgrounds. Traditional sensors use time-to-digital converters (circuits that precisely time arrival of photons) that are bulky, and frame rates are locked to the worst-case pixel condition. The authors use an event-driven approach where each pixel independently detects whether a photon arrived and adjusts its own sensitivity based on background brightness, then processes valid events asynchronously. This enables frame rates from 5 to 250 frames per second adapting to scene complexity, and reduces the need for large on-chip timing circuits.
